goal: Decide whether a contribution to a UOR Foundation project is credited to a person, following W3C PROV-O delegation from a software agent to the person it acted for.

app.name: uor-contribution-attribution
app.title: Contribution attribution
app.purpose: Permit crediting a contribution to a person in the CHAOSS contributor metrics when its PROV-O agent is a resolved person, or a software agent whose prov:actedOnBehalfOf names a resolved person with the delegation recorded in the contribution; deny unattributed software work; not applicable for organizations.

fields.name: agent
fields.means: the PROV-O agent class that made the contribution: prov:Person, prov:SoftwareAgent or prov:Organization

fields.name: identity
fields.means: whether the person credited (the agent, or its principal) is resolved to one unique contributor identity

fields.name: principal
fields.means: the PROV-O class of the agent it acted on behalf of

fields.name: trail
fields.means: whether the delegation is recorded in the contribution itself, as a commit trailer, session link or Requested by line

meanings.deny: counted as project activity but credited to no person
meanings.not-applicable: an organization's contribution, counted by organizational metrics, not person metrics
meanings.indeterminate: the person cannot be determined until their identity is resolved

rules.why: W3C PROV-O: prov:Organization is a distinct agent class; CHAOSS Organizational Diversity counts organizations, not contributors
CHAOSS Contributors: one person counted once across identities; GrimoireLab SortingHat unifies identities before counting
W3C PROV-O: prov:Person; CHAOSS Contributors counts persons who contribute
W3C PROV-O prov:actedOnBehalfOf: the delegate's activity is attributed to the responsible agent; the trail records the delegation in the contribution
W3C PROV-O: a prov:SoftwareAgent without a recorded delegation to a person is responsible for its own activity and is not a person

app.otherwiseWhy: no PROV-O path from the contribution to a person

properties.why: software work is credited to a person only by delegation
a delegation not recorded in the contribution cannot be verified from it
acting for an organization credits no person
an unresolved identity could count one person twice
a resolved person's own contribution is always credited to them

stakeholders.name: Contributor
stakeholders.text: Directs work, often through an agent, and needs it credited to them.

stakeholders.name: Agent contributor
stakeholders.text: A software agent that writes commits and pull requests and needs its work credited to the person it acted for, never counted as a person.

stakeholders.name: Community and Outreach Committee
stakeholders.text: Reads CHAOSS contributor metrics and needs persons, agents and organizations counted apart.

components.name: GrimoireLab
components.text: The CHAOSS oracle: Perceval collects contributions and SortingHat resolves identities.

components.name: Contribution trail
components.text: Commit trailers, session links and Requested by lines that record each delegation.

threats.name: Agents inflate contributor counts
threats.text: Agent commits are counted as extra people.

control.name: Delegation to a person
control.text: Software work counts only through a recorded delegation to a resolved person.

threats.name: Forged trailer
threats.text: A contribution claims a delegation from someone who never directed it.
threats.accepted: The app decides on the trail it is given; verifying a trailer's signature or session belongs to the collector and the forge.
